newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power up on cold temps return.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power up on cold temps return.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices for day-ahead delivery in the U.S. Northeast rose on forecast of cold weather returning into the region following a brief break today.
"Colder weather is supposed to be coming next week," said a New York power trader.
After snow and sleet late Thursday, today's weather moderated slightly from Thursday, with day readings in in the 20-30 degrees Fahrenheit range and night readings in the teens to 20s.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Monday delivery in the eastern part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) increased to $31.00-$32.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Thursday's range of $30.50-$31.50.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP held steady at $22.00.

In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Monday firmed to $26.00-$27.00/MWh from Thursday's $23.00-$24.00 in tandem with sharply higher prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool, where day-ahead power jumped five dollars from Thursday.
Peak, firm deliveries for Saturday and Sunday were offered at $19.50 and $18.50.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Monday was valued at $15.00-$16.00, up from Thursday's $14.50-$15.50 for Friday delivery.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border jumped to $34.00-$35.00 from Thursday's quote near $33.00/MWh.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was valued near $22.00, compared with Thursday's $21.50-$23.00.

The outlook of colder temperatures pushed cash natural gas prices higher. Swing gas deliveries at the New York City gate climbed to $4.50 per million British thermal unit level, up 50 cents from Thursday's level.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures were down 8.1 cents at $3.400/mmBtu, erasing an early 14 cent gain.
